mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays less negative while TRANSIT also rises, more commuting footfall should spill into nearby retail and recreation venues within the next month, lifting RETAIL_REC relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not average above its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days even when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived rise in GROCERY_PHARM relative to baseline indicates precautionary and convenience trips that substitute for discretionary outings, so RETAIL_REC should dip in the following week when grocery demand spikes abruptly.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by 3 points or more week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall in the next 7 days after a week-on-week GROCERY_PHARM increase of at least 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility rebounds from a depressed week, outdoor leisure trips are being reallocated away from shopping districts, so RETAIL_REC should weaken over the next two weeks after a park rebound.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by 2 points or more week-on-week from a negative baseline level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 14 days after PARKS posts a week-on-week increase of at least 2 points from below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain near or below baseline while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, the city is in a mobility-constrained regime that suppresses discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the previous four-week mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain subdued and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS combined with higher RESIDENTIAL suggests summer outdoor and at-home substitution, which should keep shopping trips subdued and push RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both remaining above their recent norms.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT after a weak week should feed retail corridors first, so RETAIL_REC should rise within two weeks when transit mobility crosses back above its recent average.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses from below its prior 2-week mean to above it
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after TRANSIT moves above its prior 2-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both rise together, households are clustering essential trips near home and avoiding discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the last four weeks in periods when GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL both increase together.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains less negative for two straight weeks while PARKS also stays below baseline, the mobility pattern implies broad reengagement without a leisure diversion, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves for two consecutive weeks while PARKS remains below 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES improves for two consecutive weeks and PARKS stays negative.
